That being said, it is also important to put virtual currency in perspective as a payment

This relative volume of transactions becomes important when you consider that,
according to the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, the best estimate for the amount of
all global criminal proceeds available for laundering through the financial system in 2009 was
$1.6 trillion.

Level 1: Confirm that the organisation’s Standard Operating Procedures have been

Level 2: Enhanced due diligence to determine and confirm the bona fides of the entity
itself as well as its owners. This includes the application of open-source information
to build a profile of these entities and then determine their level of risk. This
information includes sentiment analysis from news reports, court cases,

statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5318(g)?
statutory.answer: Yes, 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) requires reporting for these transactions.
statutory.label: entailment
statutory.reasoning: Under 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) requires reporting of transactions that have no business or apparent lawful purpose or are not the sort in which the particular customer would normally engage. The fact pattern shows Entity SYN_28f97744, a business with an expected monthly volume of $11,632,908, processed six transactions in three days totaling over $86 million, which vastly exceeds its declared volume. Furthermore, the notes explicitly identify these transactions as 'peel-chain hop,' a technique commonly associated with money laundering to obscure the source of funds. Because the volume is inconsistent with the KYC profile and the activity indicates layering, the conduct triggers the reporting requirements of 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g).

sar_output.suspicious_activity_report: Entity SYN_28f97744 exhibited a rapid-movement layering pattern consistent with a peel-chain. Between 2026-04-25 and 2026-04-28, the entity executed six wire transfers to various counterparties (including WHU Capital LLC and MAN Solutions LLC) totaling $86,515,340.23. This volume vastly exceeds the entity's declared expected monthly volume of $11,632,908.00. The transactions show a descending amount pattern (from $15.9M to $13.0M), which aligns with the 'peel-chain' typology described in SOP-LAYERING-01. This activity is inconsistent with the entity's declared business purpose as a virtual asset service provider and triggers reporting requirements under 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g). We defer the final filing decision to the human investigator.
